chromium.thesis: Total chromium and hexavalent chromium are separate required measurements. Cr(VI) is an IARC Group 1 carcinogen on occupational-inhalation evidence and is assessed by US EPA as likely carcinogenic by the oral route; the absence of a food-specific government maximum is an evidence and standards gap, not proof that chromium is immaterial.
chromium.toxicology_replace_tail: EFSA, the US EPA, IARC, and California OEHHA converge on the same species distinction: Cr(VI) carries the principal hazard while Cr(III) is much less toxic. That distinction does not justify omitting either measurement. Total chromium provides the mass-balance and contamination signal; speciated Cr(VI) provides the hazard-specific result. Where food law supplies no numeric ceiling, HMTc must derive and disclose a program limit through its governed standards method rather than label the analyte not material.
chromium.occurrence_prose_replace_tail: Total-chromium occurrence cannot be read as a Cr(VI) exposure estimate, but it remains a required control rather than a substitute or a reason to omit chromium. HMTc therefore requires a numeric total-chromium ceiling and a separate numeric Cr(VI) ceiling for every product standard. Occurrence evidence anchors the total-chromium control; species-specific evidence anchors the Cr(VI) control. Until both values are derived and published, the affected standard is incomplete.
chromium.how_regulated: No government food code currently supplies a comprehensive pair of maximum levels for total chromium and Cr(VI) across HMTc product matrices. Adjacent enforceable instruments include California's 10 µg/L drinking-water maximum contaminant level for Cr(VI), the US EPA and California total-chromium drinking-water limits, and Proposition 65 safe-harbor levels; those are not food concentration limits and cannot be copied into a food row without a documented conversion and applicability judgment. Regulatory silence is recorded as a gap. It is not evidence that chromium is immaterial and it does not satisfy the requirement for a numeric HMTc limit.
chromium.hmtc_treatment: HMTc treats total chromium and hexavalent chromium as two required, non-substitutable analytes. Every product-category standard must publish a numeric total-Cr limit and a separate numeric Cr(VI) limit in the product's native basis. A total-Cr screen, a reflex-speciation trigger, a dash, or an n/m designation does not satisfy either missing value. Where no directly applicable government ceiling exists, the limits remain unresolved until the governed evidence-pooling and standards-setting process derives auditable values; the page is visibly flagged incomplete in the meantime.

species_pages.name: Hexavalent chromium
species_pages.thesis: Hexavalent chromium is a species-specific required analyte because it is an IARC Group 1 carcinogen on occupational-inhalation evidence and US EPA assesses it as likely carcinogenic by the oral route. A total-chromium result cannot establish the Cr(VI) concentration, and the lack of a food-specific government maximum does not establish immateriality.
